claims.text: The initial alloy has a non-equilibrium microstructure containing metastable solid solutions and intermetallic compounds.
The initial alloy contains Mg-rich regions.
The alloy density is below 6 g/cm³.
Sub-melting thermal ageing permits Mg diffusion from the metastable matrix.
Mg diffusion during thermal ageing promotes transformation of metastable phases into stable Mg-rich intermetallic compounds.
The Mg-rich intermetallic compounds formed during ageing are thermodynamically more stable than the initial metastable phases.
Stable Mg-rich intermetallic compounds act as nucleation sites for protective oxide-scale formation.
Ageing-induced microstructural evolution promotes formation of a continuous, adherent oxide scale rich in Mg species during subsequent high-temperature oxidation.
The aged alloy will contain more stable Mg-rich intermetallic phase than the as-cast alloy.
The aged alloy will form a more uniform and protective high-temperature oxide scale than the as-cast alloy.
The ageing-induced oxide-scale and microstructural changes will produce a measurable change in corrosion resistance relative to the as-cast state.
The proposed mechanism applies when Mg is a significant constituent and ageing permits Mg diffusion without melting or deleterious transformations.
